findings.explanation: HOL4 saves only HD (h::t) = h. The definition goes through Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition, i.e. new_specification (Defn.sml:1192, Prim_rec.sml:281), so no saved equation fixes HD []. I found no saved theorem about HD [] in the list sources. In HOL4, ARB is an unconstrained constant (boolScript.sml:245). Lean proves HD [] = ARB, and hence EL 0 [] = ARB and, with LAST, HD [] = LAST []. HOL4 leaves all of these open. Differing input: [].
findings.repair:
def HD {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : List α → α
  | h :: _ => h
  | [] => Classical.epsilon (fun f : List α → α => ∀ h t, f (h :: t) = h) []
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.List

example : HOL.HD ([] : List Nat) = HOL.ARB := by simp only [HOL.HD]

findings.explanation: HOL4's LAST_DEF has only the clause LAST (h::t) = if t = [] then h else LAST t. It is made by new_recursive_definition, i.e. new_specification. The saved theorems I found (LAST_CONS, LAST_EL, LAST_compute, ...) concern nonempty lists, so LAST [] is open. Lean adds LAST [] = ARB and so proves that equation, and also LAST [] = HD [], which HOL4 leaves open. Differing input: [].
findings.repair:
def LAST {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : List α → α
  | [] => Classical.epsilon (fun f : List α → α => ∀ h t, f (h :: t) = if t = [] then h else f t) []
  | h :: t => if t = [] then h else LAST t
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.List

example : HOL.LAST ([] : List Nat) = HOL.ARB := by simp only [HOL.LAST]
findings.hol4_check: !c:'a. ?last. (!h t. last (h::t) = if t = [] then h else last t) /\ (last [] = c)
